scenes.heading: Fact Tables
scenes.narration: A fact table is the heart of a dimensional model, storing the measurable events of a business.

scenes.heading: Anatomy of a fact table
bullets: Measures: the numeric values you analyze, like revenue.
Foreign keys: links to each descriptive dimension.
Grain: the exact meaning of one row.
Usually tall and narrow, with billions of rows.
scenes.narration: Every fact table stores measures, the numbers you sum and average, alongside foreign keys pointing to dimensions. Its grain defines precisely what one row represents, such as one line item on one order. Because events accumulate endlessly, fact tables grow tall and narrow.

scenes.heading: Designing a fact table
scenes.narration: The first and most important step is declaring the grain, because everything else depends on it. Once you know what one row means, you choose the dimensions that give it context and the measures you will aggregate. Finally you wire in foreign keys so the fact connects to its dimensions.

scenes.heading: Fact types
scenes.narration: A transaction fact records each event as it happens, and its measures add up cleanly across any dimension. A snapshot fact captures state at intervals, so measures like account balance are only additive across some dimensions, not time. Knowing the type tells you how safely you can sum a column.

scenes.heading: A transaction-grain fact
scenes.code:
CREATE TABLE fact_sales (
  sale_id      BIGINT,
  date_key     INT NOT NULL,
  product_key  INT NOT NULL,
  store_key    INT NOT NULL,
  quantity     INT,
  sales_amount DECIMAL(12,2)  -- additive measure
);
scenes.narration: Each row here is one sale, so the grain is a single transaction. The three keys connect it to the date, product, and store dimensions. The quantity and sales amount are additive, meaning they can be summed across any combination of those dimensions safely.

scenes.text: Fact tables hold the numbers you measure and the keys that connect them to dimensions, all anchored by a clearly declared grain.
scenes.narration: Declare the grain before anything else, and the rest of the fact table design falls naturally into place.
